Link

A text link to another view or another site: in running text, standing alone, external or quiet.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • To go to another view, another place in this view or another site.
  • In running text, as a plain a element with no class.
  • Standing alone, such as View all runs under a list, with the ds-link class.
  • With the external-link icon and the hidden hint when the link opens another site in a new tab.

When not to use it

  • For an action that changes something, such as Delete branch or Retry. Use a button.
  • For the main action of a view, even when it goes to another view. Use a link with the primary button classes.
  • For the app's main destinations. Use a tab bar, or the sidebar at 768px and wider.
  • For something unavailable. A link cannot be disabled, so write plain text and say why it is unavailable.

Variants

inline
A link inside a sentence. It takes no class: the base styles underline it, and it has the colour of the text around it.
standalone ds-link
A link outside a sentence. It is 44px tall and may end with an icon, such as arrow-right.
quiet ds-link--quiet
With ds-link, for a minor link that should not draw the eye, such as Edit approval rules. Muted, and still underlined.
external
Not a class but a pattern, for a link with target="_blank": end it with a ds-link__icon showing external-link and a ds-link__hint holding (opens in a new tab). It works in an inline, a standalone and a quiet link.

Sizes

default
A standalone link takes the text size around it and is at least 44px tall and wide. An inline link is the size of its sentence.

Accessibility

  • Use an a element with an href. Without an href it cannot be reached with the keyboard.
  • The link text names where it goes and makes sense read alone: the log for run 2291, never here or read more.
  • A link is underlined in every variant and state. Do not remove the underline, and do not mark a link by colour alone.
  • A link that opens a new tab says so. Put (opens in a new tab) in a ds-link__hint inside the link, which a screen reader reads and the screen does not show, and set rel="noopener".
  • An icon inside a link is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true". The external-link icon is the visible sign of what the hint says.
  • Tab moves to the link and Enter follows it. Space does not, which is one reason an action is a button.
  • A standalone link has a 44px pointer target. An inline link is exempt, so do not put two of them side by side in a sentence.
